blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Prehistoric India covers the Palaeolithic, Mesolithic, and Neolithic ages marked by stone tool evolution and site settlements.
The Indus Valley Civilization featured advanced town planning, unique scripts, and extensive trade networks.
The Vedic transition from Early to Later periods witnessed significant shifts in socio-political structure and religion.
The 6th century BCE saw the rise of 16 Mahajanapadas alongside influential heterodox movements like Buddhism and Jainism.
Prominent empires like the Mauryans, Guptas, Mughals, and Vijayanagar established distinct systems of administration and culture.

blocks.content: 6. EARLY VEDIC vs LATER VEDIC (MOST IMPORTANT)
CHAPTER 5: MAURYAN EMPIRE TO GUPTA EMPIRE
IMPORTANT DEVELOPMENTS DURING EARLY MEDIEVAL PERIOD

rows: Tribal chiefdoms (Rajan); democratic tribal assemblies (Sabha, Samiti) held power
Larger territorial kingdoms (Janapadas); monarchical authority strengthened
Flexible Varna system based on occupation; better status for women
Rigid birth-based Varna system; decline in the position of women
Pastoral economy dominated by cattle rearing
Agarian economy with settled agriculture becoming primary

blocks.content: 4. IMPORTANT BATTLES OF THE MUGHAL PERIOD

items: Differences between Early Vedic and Later Vedic administrative and social structures are frequently tested.
Details regarding Buddhist Councils, Tripitaka literature, and Jain Great Vows carry high exam weightage.
Major decisive battles such as Plassey (1757), Buxar (1764), and Talikota (1565) are recurring direct questions.
Chronology of European arrivals, Governor-Generals' land revenue policies, and events of the 1857 Revolt are critical for one-liner questions.
